mechanism_narrative: A sustained month-over-month increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) exceeding 0.5% indicates strengthening labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS increases by at least 0.5% month-over-month, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.5% for two consecutive months signals aggressive monetary easing that lowers discount rates and stimulates equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered periods, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in retail sales (RSAFS) by at least 0.5% month-over-month and decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by at least 0.25% month-over-month indicates strong consumer demand coupled with accommodative monetary policy, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: monetary easing with strong consumer demand
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS rises by at least 0.5% and FEDFUNDS falls by at least 0.25% month-over-month, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansions characterized by housing starts (HOUST) above 900 thousand units and unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5.0%, elevated consumer confidence and spending drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods during late-cycle expansions (HOUST > 900 and UNRATE < 5.0%), or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 0.3% signals accelerating inflation that typically triggers monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL rises by at least 0.3% month-over-month, or the Rank IC is above -0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) exceeds 102.0 for two consecutive months, it signals robust manufacturing growth that correlates with rising corporate profits, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered periods, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In high labor market tightness regimes (UNRATE below 5.0% and PAYEMS growth above 0.5% month-over-month), wage pressures support consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods during high labor market tightness (UNRATE < 5.0% and PAYEMS growth > 0.5% MoM), or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) by at least 0.5% month-over-month and industrial production (INDPRO) by at least 0.3% month-over-month indicates strong demand for consumer and durable goods, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST rises by at least 0.5% and INDPRO rises by at least 0.3% month-over-month, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
